METHODOLOGY_SECTION_OR_RULE: Section C/D (mandatory scenario families / materiality screening)
AMBIGUITY_DESCRIPTION: The methodology mandates screening every feature against all 19 scenario families but does not specify whether the register must contain an explicit row for every screened-nonmaterial family-feature pairing (up to 19x23=437 rows) or only for families that clear the materiality threshold, with screening-out documented at a summary level.
REVIEWER_B_PROVISIONAL_TREATMENT: Reviewer B performed the full 19-family analytical screen for each of the 23 features but registered only the families that cleared a materiality trigger (MATERIAL_SCENARIO_CONFIRMED or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_RETAINED). Screened-nonmaterial families are not given individual register rows; the disposition is summarized narratively in Report Section 3.
NOTES: A second reviewer choosing full 437-row registration would produce a materially larger, differently-shaped register even if underlying judgments matched.

AMBIGUITY_DESCRIPTION: The Matrix CSV's implementation-evidence taxonomy (IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED, PARTIAL_IMPLEMENTATION, DOCUMENTED_ONLY) does not map 1:1 onto the methodology's six control-effectiveness states (VERIFIED_EFFECTIVE, PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED, DESIGNED_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, ABSENT, UNKNOWN, NOT_APPLICABLE). In particular, PARTIAL_IMPLEMENTATION could plausibly be read as either IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED (partial code exists, unverified) or PARTIALLY_VERIFIED (implying some verification occurred), which have different credit ceilings (LIMITED_OPERATING_CREDIT vs SUPPORTED_OPERATING_CREDIT).
REVIEWER_B_PROVISIONAL_TREATMENT: Reviewer B mapped PARTIAL_IMPLEMENTATION to IMPLEMENTED_UNVERIFIED (conservative reading) because IMPLEMENTATION_TEST_AND_EVIDENCE_STATUS_SUMMARY.csv records test_verified=0 and runtime_verified=0 for every domain with no exception, so no domain has any accepted verification event regardless of the matrix's 'partial' label. This keeps all five affected features at LIMITED_OPERATING_CREDIT rather than SUPPORTED.
NOTES: A reviewer reading PARTIAL_IMPLEMENTATION as PARTIALLY_VERIFIED would assign SUPPORTED_OPERATING_CREDIT to 5 features, potentially justifying a residual-severity reduction the methodology otherwise forbids without evidenced control linkage.

AMBIGUITY_DESCRIPTION: The methodology defines five governance-urgency labels but does not specify a mapping from the Matrix's own governance-coverage-state taxonomy (OPERATING_STANDARD_GAP, PIA_SUPPLEMENT_CANDIDATE, CODE_GUIDE_GAP, ADR_GAP, RUNBOOK_GAP, NEW_PIA_CANDIDATE, COVERED_WITH_RETAINED_GAP) onto those five labels, so no basis exists to differentiate urgency across features by gap type (e.g., is NEW_PIA_CANDIDATE with NO_CURRENT_PIA_OWNER_IDENTIFIED more urgent than COVERED_WITH_RETAINED_GAP).
REVIEWER_B_PROVISIONAL_TREATMENT: Reviewer B applied DEFERRED uniformly at ES-SCOPE-CURRENT-PREPRODUCTION (nothing is currently live or reachable, per README_FIRST and the evidence summary) and PRE_ACTIVATION_REQUIRED uniformly at ES-SCOPE-AUTHORIZED-FUTURE-ACTIVATION (Founder decision required = YES for essentially every one of the 23 features), without differentiating by governance-coverage-state subtype.
EVIDENCE_REFS: SELECTED_FEATURE_POPULATION.csv Founder-decision column; feature_full_briefs.txt governance coverage state field per feature
NOTES: This uniform treatment is a defensible floor but may understate relative urgency differences between, e.g., a feature with zero PIA owner at all (Marketplace, Developer) versus one with only a retained documentation gap (Identity).

AMBIGUITY_DESCRIPTION: No concrete authorization plan, timeline, or Founder decision date exists anywhere in the package for any feature. It is unclear whether ACTIVATION_PROXIMITY should be reported as NOT_AUTHORIZED (the accurate present-day fact, applied identically regardless of scope) or as a forward-looking label such as PLANNED_LATER/UNKNOWN when populating the row for the ES-SCOPE-AUTHORIZED-FUTURE-ACTIVATION governance-horizon scope specifically.
REVIEWER_B_PROVISIONAL_TREATMENT: Reviewer B used NOT_AUTHORIZED uniformly for both scopes, treating it as a present-day fact rather than fabricating a plan or timeline that is not evidenced anywhere in the package.
NOTES: This choice does not change any severity/likelihood/score value; it only affects the ACTIVATION_PROXIMITY field's descriptive framing.

METHODOLOGY_SECTION_OR_RULE: Section D (materiality dispositions) / Section I (calibration states)
AMBIGUITY_DESCRIPTION: Three features carry an AI_DECISION_IMPACT=MATERIAL_DECISION_SUPPORT_REVIEW_REQUIRED flag with no elaborating description of the underlying AI mechanism or its review control. It is unclear whether such a bare flag, with no descriptive elaboration, is sufficient basis to register a distinct scenario at all (versus being folded silently into the feature's primary scenario as a note, or dropped as too speculative to register).
REVIEWER_B_PROVISIONAL_TREATMENT: Reviewer B registered a separate scenario with MATERIALITY_DISPOSITION=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_RETAINED and CALIBRATION_STATE=INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (blank score, RISK_PRIORITY_SIGNAL=EVIDENCE_REVIEW_REQUIRED) for each, under the materiality trigger 'evidence insufficient but plausible material consequence cannot responsibly be dismissed' (Section D), rather than silently dropping or fabricating detail.
EVIDENCE_REFS: feature_full_briefs.txt AI_DECISION_IMPACT field for ES-FEAT-INTEGRATIONS-001, ES-FEAT-AI-001, ES-FEAT-INVENTORY-001
NOTES: This treatment is defensible under the existing rule text and does not require a rule change, but a second reviewer could reasonably fold these into primary-scenario notes instead.

AMBIGUITY_DESCRIPTION: The methodology permits INHERENT_RISK_LIKELIHOOD to be NOT_MEANINGFULLY_ESTIMABLE 'where a useful counterfactual cannot be established' but does not specify when this applies versus when a reviewer should estimate a distinct no-control-credit inherent likelihood value.
REVIEWER_B_PROVISIONAL_TREATMENT: Reviewer B used NOT_MEANINGFULLY_ESTIMABLE uniformly for INHERENT_RISK_LIKELIHOOD across all 27 calibrated scenario identities, reasoning that a true zero-controls architectural counterfactual is not meaningfully constructible for a software feature, and used the assessed value only for RESIDUAL_LIKELIHOOD.
NOTES: Does not change any RISK_SCORE value since scores are computed from residual, not inherent, likelihood.
